chunks: Maysir asked al-Sadiq عليه السلام about a man who entered ihram from al-‘Aqiq and another who entered ihram from al-Kufah: which of the two had performed the better deed? So he said:
"O Maysir, is it better that you pray al-‘Asr as four, or that you pray it as six?"
I said: "I pray it as four."
He عليه السلام said: "Thus, the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is better than anything else."

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered into ihram for hajj or ‘umrah
key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: better or more excellent in deed
key_terms.الْعَقِيقِ: al-‘Aqiq, the appointed miqat mentioned in this ruling
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: al-Kufah, the alternative place mentioned for entering ihram
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.سُنَّةُ: the normative practice and prophetic tradition

ai.seo_question: Is entering ihram from the prescribed miqat better than entering it earlier from al-Kufah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that acting in accordance with the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is superior to adopting an alternative practice, even if one might imagine it to be more rigorous. In the context of entering ihram, the Imam عليه السلام affirms that beginning from the prescribed miqat of al-‘Aqiq is better than beginning earlier from al-Kufah.
